SpernerNDim.lean is complete (669 lines, 0 sorries): structure SpernerTriangulation (8 fields) + theorem sperner_ndim (line 654) which yields a fully-colored simplex from an odd count of last-face boundary doors. This is the exact finish line for sperner_grid.

Last-face boundary doors of the d-grid are in bijection with panchromatic (d-1)-simplices of the induced (d-1)-Freudenthal grid on face d: adj=none + boundary_face puts the facet on face d; the Sperner condition forbids color d there; isDoorAt = all colors {0..d-1} present = IsFC for the (d-1)-grid. Induction + sperner_parity at d-1 gives oddness. Base d=0: count 1.

Coordinate bridge: abstract framework uses Vertex d N (Fin d -> N, sum<=N, Kuhn coords); SpernerGrid uses BaryPoint d N (Fin (d+1) -> N, sum=N). They are canonically isomorphic; proving BaryPoint d N ≃ Vertex d N (~30-50 lines, no adjacency) is the cleanest standalone first deliverable and unlocks reuse of the whole framework.

Phase-1 instance must use unoriented Kuhn cells (base point + permutation of increment order, one representative per geometric cell). The Session-1 orientation-doubling bug came from carrying a free miss/orientation flag in GridSimplex; the instance must NOT.

Session 5: representation A (GridSimplex subtype) preferred over Finset for the Phase-1 Simplex type — Finset does not dodge the canonical vertex-ordering obligation; IsCanon s := forall k, lex (s.verts 0) <= s.verts k is a simpler computable canonicality predicate (step_dec fixes chain direction from lex-min base).

Phase-1 GridSimplex-rep REQUIRES canonicalization: a facet-sharing dual graph over all GridSimplices breaks adj_unique_facet (a cell and its reverse share the same vertex set/facets). Cube-Kuhn lex-min-base uniqueness does NOT transfer (corner-simplex is not a union of full Kuhn cubes), so a separate IsCanon predicate is mandatory.

The chain-interior facet (delete vertex a.succ, 0<a.succ<d) always has a neighbour: swap the two consecutive increment steps a,b (b.castSucc=a.succ). Only the middle vertex moves to the opposite corner verts(a.castSucc)+e_{incDir b}-e_miss; the miss coordinate is untouched at every vertex (so step_dec is inherited verbatim), and only steps a,b have a moved endpoint. This is the GridSimplex-level EXISTENCE half of the search-based adj boundary_face obligation (an interior facet must have a partner).
Pitfall: subst hka with hka:k=a eliminates a (replacing a by k), not k — breaks references to the def binder a. Use rw [hka] (and rw [hka] at hjI ⊢) instead to keep a.
Pitfall: nat (x+1)+0 is defeq x+1, so rw/simp auto-closes such goals by rfl — a trailing omega then errors with No goals.

Carrier repair (d≥2): the lex-min IsCanon carrier omits cells (#31156); use GridSimplex directly — existence definitional, uniqueness via eq_of_range_eq. grid_eq_of_vertices_range is the sound replacement for canon_eq_of_vertices_range (PR #31163, 0-axiom).

The facet/adj bookkeeping (facet_card, facet_injective, facet_unique_neighbor, facet_vertex_injective) is now available on the SOUND GridSimplex carrier for d≥2, with proofs identical to the CanonSimplex versions modulo vertices→gridVertices and canon_eq_of_vertices_range→grid_eq_of_vertices_range hd. The crux gridFacet_unique_neighbor (adj_unique_facet) no longer relies on the cell-omitting CanonSimplex carrier (#31156 existence failure).

Geometric boundary faces of a Freudenthal cell are LOCALIZED to the top facet: for d≥2, if facet k satisfies the boundary-coordinate condition (∀ j≠k, (verts j).coords k = 0) then k = Fin.last d (boundary_face_imp_last). Every facet is miss (excluded by miss_not_boundary_face) or an increase direction incDir c (incDir_boundary_face_imp_last forces incDir c = Fin.last d, since the last chain vertex value d would need d ≤ c.val < d).

Facet 0 is NEVER a geometric boundary face for d≥2 (zero_not_boundary_face). So gridNeighbor sending BOTH {0, Fin.last d} to none is a within-chain artifact: the GEOMETRIC none-fibre is at most the singleton {Fin.last d}, strictly inside the index-level IsBoundaryFacet set {0,last}. This pins the exact obligation the cross-chain gluing frontier owes: facet 0 (interior to Δ_N) must carry a cross-Kuhn pivot partner (never a genuine ∂Δ_N door).

Session 18: the same-miss facet-0 pivot (zeroPivotCell) is a monotone descent in the shared miss coordinate — partner base_miss = base_miss - 1 (its base is s.verts 1, one chain-step down; miss_coord_at).

Pivot chain terminates exactly at base_miss = d (the extremal cell whose top vertex sits on the geometric miss-face): infeasible <=> base_miss = d; partner re-feasible <=> base_miss >= d+2. This is the discrete path structure the Phase-2 door-parity induction runs on.

Reciprocity (crux 1 core): the top-facet (Fin.last d) pivot on the partner t=zeroPivotCell s reintroduces exactly s deleted apex s.verts 0 — pinned coordinate-wise via step_inc/step_dec/step_same at k=0; this is the inverse the adj partial involution needs at the boundary facets

Dual-pivot distinctness: the top-facet pivot's new base vertex leaves the cell in the lastIncDir=incDir(d-1) coordinate (value base-1 vs chain min base). coord_incDir_at makes chain-monotonicity of any incDir coordinate a one-liner (base + [step already fired]). Pairs with the existing zeroPivotTop_not_mem_chain (facet-0 side) — both boundary pivots produce genuinely-new vertices, the distinctness half of adj being a boundary partial involution.

Session 22: cell-level reciprocity topPivotCell (zeroPivotCell s) = s follows almost entirely from index bookkeeping once the vertex-0 identity (topPivotBottom_zeroPivotCell) is in hand — zeroPivotCell shifts s's chain UP by one (verts k = s.verts (k+1)) and appends a new apex, while topPivotCell shifts back DOWN (verts (k>=1) = t.verts (k-1)) and prepends a new base; the two shifts compose to the identity on indices >=1, vertex 0 is the reciprocal-base identity, and the two cyclic incDir rotations (deferred-incDir-0 vs lastIncDir-first) are mutually inverse. No new geometry — the two boundary pivots are a genuine partial involution at the shared facet.
